extracted.intended_audience: Federal regional and field staff and agency officials responsible for Tribal consultation and decision-making
extracted.subtask_description: Best-practices guidance for federal regional and field staff on identifying and protecting Tribal treaty rights, reserved rights, and similar rights when planning, notifying, and conducting Tribal consultation and related federal decision-making. Covers legal principles, consultation procedures, notice and materials, interagency coordination, Indigenous Knowledge, recordkeeping, mapping, and staff training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful consultation (overarching standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribal consultation should be meaningful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A meaningful consultation is, among other inclusive practices: carried out in a timely, efficient, and responsive manner; transparent and predictable; accessible, reasonable, flexible, and fair; founded in the principles of good faith and respectful of the sovereignty of Indian Tribes; and includes reasonable accommodation (e.g., changing of timelines, project parameters), where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity of federal consultation policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Tribal consultation policies should strive for uniformity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use common definitions, processes, and time frames for consistency, ease of Tribal use, and to promote a whole-of-government approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of Tribal sovereignty and self-governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribes are sovereign nations with self-governance and self-determination rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recognition applies to all Tribes (not limited to those with specific self-determination contracts) and frames the Nation-to-Nation relationship with the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nation-to-Nation relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribes have a two-way Nation-to-Nation relationship with the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation should reflect and respect this bilateral, sovereign-to-sovereign relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal initiation of consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribal consultation may be initiated at the request of a Tribal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should respond to requests for consultation within a reasonable time and undertake analyses even when Tribes do not request consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treaties as substantive federal law
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribal treaties are substantive federal law and do not derive from other federal statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treaties may explicitly or implicitly secure rights (land, fishing, hunting, water, goods/services); they are interpreted as grants of rights from Tribes and reservations of rights not granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supremacy of treaties
rubrics_metrics.description: Treaties, like the U.S. Constitution and federal statutes, are the supreme law of the land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must treat applicable treaties as binding legal agreements between sovereign nations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust relationship and fiduciary obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The general trust relationship exists between the United States and Indian Tribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The government 'has charged itself with moral obligations of the highest responsibility and trust.' The nature of trust duties is defined by federal law and may include particular duties or fiduciary obligations relevant to consultation and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency notice, coordination, and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation policies should incorporate processes for notifying, coordinating, and collaborating with other federal agencies when multiple agencies have a vested interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially important when actions implicate multiple Tribes and/or multiple Tribal treaties; agencies should identify and notify potentially relevant departments and coordinate their collaboration in consultation and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful consideration of Tribal information and seeking consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Information obtained from Tribes must be given meaningful consideration and agencies should strive for consensus or a mutually desired outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies should acknowledge that Tribal information will be given meaningful consideration, and ensure it is solicited early enough to potentially influence decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of federal decision-makers with authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultations should generally include federal and Tribal officials with decision-making authorities regarding the proposed policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The head of each agency should ensure federal representatives with appropriate expertise and, to the extent practicable, decision-making authority are present at Nation-to-Nation consultations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize official Tribal leaders and verify authority of speakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should prioritize participation by official Tribal government leaders and verify whether non-official sources have authority to speak for the Tribal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If federal agencies receive information from a source other than a Tribal government official, they should ascertain appropriate Tribal authority by communicating directly with Tribal government officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop mutually agreed upon consultation protocols with each Tribe
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should develop, where possible, mutually agreed consultation protocols that accommodate Tribally enacted consultation laws, statutes, policies, or protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees of federal agencies and Tribal Nations should maintain open channels of communication and share information. Less formal engagement is not a substitute for formal consultation. Agencies are required to respect and elevate Indigenous Knowledge (IK), including cultural norms and practices relevant to consultations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify Tribes how their input influenced decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribal consultation policies should identify the process for notifying Tribes of how Tribal input influenced federal decision-making after consultation concludes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each agency should disclose to affected Tribes the outcome of consultation and decisions made as a result in a timely manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply principles to the extent practicable and permitted by law
rubrics_metrics.description: All principles and best practices should be applied to the extent practicable and permitted by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes legal limits while urging implementation whenever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin early (timing of consultation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation should begin early in project, policy, or other federal action planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consult potentially affected Tribes before decisions are made, undertake an early analysis to determine whether consultation is required or appropriate, and respond to Tribal requests within a reasonable time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish protocols ahead of time
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should develop consultation protocols ahead of time to formalize how consultation will occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocols should ensure effective notice, establish minimum consultation periods and timelines for written comments, ensure appropriate access, and provide for agency follow-up. Agencies should inquire about and be respectful of Indigenous Knowledge and Tribally developed consultation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to consult (triggers and assessment questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is any question whether an agency policy will have Tribal implications, consultation should be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should assess whether Tribal treaty, reserved, or similar rights are affected by proposed action. Key questions: Do treaties/reserved rights exist that are implicated? What Tribal treaty-protected resources rely upon the area? How might rights be affected?

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the appropriate federal decisionmaker for consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the subject matter, agencies should ensure federal representatives with appropriate expertise and decision-making authority regarding the proposed policy are present during consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures consultations are substantive and that discussions can meaningfully influence outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating effective notice (timeliness and methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation should be scheduled so Tribes are provided timely, adequate notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To the extent practicable, notice should be sent at least 30 days in advance (most Tribes recommend 60 days). Use Dear Tribal Leader letters, Federal Register notices, and agency websites. Maintain a single comprehensive electronic list of Tribal governmental leadership to receive notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include read-ahead materials with notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation notices should include all pertinent information about the consultation topic (agenda, framing paper, relevant legal or other documents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials could include draft proposals, analyses, and initiatives; identify the agency’s current understanding of implicated treaty/reserved rights and invite Tribal response to better inform agency decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of consultation opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should provide consultation opportunities that are accessible and convenient to Tribal participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider location, timing, language, technology access, and other barriers to participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify appropriate Tribal participants broadly
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should notify and invite all potentially affected Tribes to consult, including Tribes with historical or cultural connections to the project area regardless of their current location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that tribal traditional and historical lands may be far from reservations and that off-reservation hunting/fishing rights may apply to non-ceded lands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat information from Tribes as potentially influential
rubrics_metrics.description: Information obtained from Tribes should be given meaningful consideration, but only if Tribes are properly informed and input is solicited early enough to influence decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures that consultation is not perfunctory; timing and adequacy of information provided to Tribes affect influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify authority of non-Tribal government sources
rubrics_metrics.description: When agencies receive information during consultation from a source other than a Tribal government official, the agency should ascertain whether that source has appropriate Tribal authority to speak for the Tribal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do so by communicating directly with Tribal government officials before relying on such information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency consultations and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and notify all potentially relevant departments and agencies that may have an interest in a proposed action and coordinate their collaboration in consultation and decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps present a unified federal position and ensures all agency interests and legal obligations are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treaty research pre-consultation (comprehensive review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should seek to review every treaty into which a Tribe has entered when conducting research for consultation related to treaty or reserved rights (not only the most recent treaty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand historical context and identify potential rights, resources, or impacted historical lands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use established treaty databases to identify potentially impacted treaties
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should utilize established Tribal treaty databases to identify treaties that may be affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: Oklahoma State Tribal Treaty Database and National Archives Digital Tribal Treaty Database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indigenous Knowledge (IK) guidance and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should consider opportunities to apply Indigenous Knowledge consistent with Tribal direction and follow a dialogue to identify proposed applications, benefits, and risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform Tribes that some federal laws (e.g., FOIA) may require disclosure of information; take measures to preserve confidentiality of sensitive IK consistent with Tribal direction and the law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making materials should include Indians Canons of Construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefing materials for decisionmakers should include the Indians Canons of Construction and relevant judicial positions on treaty interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal officials should endeavor to interpret Tribal treaty and reserved rights as they would have been understood by Tribes at signing, and recognize that ambiguous treaty provisions are to be interpreted in the Tribe’s favor, in consultation with the Tribe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider multiple perspectives in disputed rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the existence, nature, or scope of an asserted Tribal right is not clearly established or is disputed, agencies should carefully consider information and views provided by Tribes and coordinate internally and with other agencies before addressing disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge disputes between Tribes or third parties and avoid unilateral resolutions without coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of consultation and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a record of the consultation process for consultations required under E.O. 13175.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record must include a summary of Tribal input received; an explanation of how Tribal input influenced or was incorporated; and reasoning for why Tribal suggestions were not incorporated or why consensus could not be attained. Disclose outcomes to affected Tribes, protect information designated sensitive by Tribes to the extent permitted by law, and consider publicly posting records for national/regional consultations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map areas of agency operations in consultation with Tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should map the spaces in which they operate to illustrate where agency actions may impact Tribal treaty rights, reserved rights, or similar rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapping may consider locations of agency installations/offices, physical territory administered or managed, areas where agency licenses/permits/funds actions, which Tribes may have cultural/ancestral connections, and what Tribes' natural or cultural resources may be implicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for federal staff on consultations and treaties
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agency staff should be trained on appropriate consultation protocols, Tribal treaty rights, reserved rights, and working with Tribal governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional and field staff should receive regular annual trainings on treaties for the geographic areas they serve; agencies should develop regional trainings in consultation and coordination with Tribes in those service areas.
